Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo and the time today. Quick recap from our discovery to make sure we’re aligned on the Dedicated capacity sizing inputs so the infra team can build an initial proposal:

Summary of current ask (from call):
- Target workloads: interactive chat and short-form generation for customer support flows + some batch inference for analytics.
- Preferred deployment mode: Dedicated capacity (data isolation + predictable throughput).
- Target latency SLO: 95th pct first-token <= 400 ms for interactive flows.

Questions / sizing inputs we discussed (please confirm):
1) Models: primary model is an open LLM (13B-class) with occasional fallback to a larger 33B variant for complex cases.
2) TPS targets: sustained ~20 requests/sec, peak up to ~60 req/sec (short spikes up to 90s).
3) Concurrency: median concurrent sessions ~40, peak concurrent ~150.
4) Token mix: ~30% short (<=64 tokens), ~50% medium (<=256 tokens), ~20% long (>=1024 tokens).
   - Avg prompt tokens: ~120
   - Avg completion tokens: ~350
   - Avg total tokens/request ≈ 470
5) Latency tolerance: interactive paths need lower latency (see SLO above); batch jobs are best-effort.
6) Data residency: US-only (no cross-region).
7) Security/compliance: SOC2 required; procurement will request questionnaire and evidence (we can attach our SOC2 pack).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Aditya and Rafael will take the numbers above and map to an initial Dedicated pool config (GPU type, pool size, buffer for burst, autoscale policy) and share a sizing spreadsheet.
- Marissa will loop in procurement to start contract/terms once sizing/cost looks OK.

I attached our dedicated sizing template (RI-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) with the fields we’ll populate. Can you confirm the TPS/concurrency/token-mix numbers above or correct them inline?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Jordan — good color. A few notes from infra sizing perspective (quick, high-level):

1) GPU type: Given the 13B baseline and the occasional 33B fallback, and the need for sub-500ms P95 first-token, our recommendation is H100 80GB for the primary pool. H100 gives a better headroom for larger sequences and more efficient batching for your token mix. If cost pressures come up we can size on A100 80GB as a lower-cost alternative but may need more instances.

2) Initial pool estimate: to meet sustained 20 TPS with your avg ~470 tokens/request and the 13B model, a conservative starting point is 3 H100s with a small buffer for burst (autoscale + 1 extra node). For the 33B fallback we can either run 1-2 dedicated H100s or route fallback to a smaller pool of 2xH100 that can be scaled up during known maintenance windows.

3) Peak/burst handling: we recommend autoscale thresholds at 70% GPU utilization and a short burst buffer of +2 nodes to absorb spikes to 90+ TPS. Also use intelligent batching + KV prefix caching for the support flows to reduce per-token compute.

4) Concurrency: because most peak concurrency is short-lived, we’ll tune the RPC timeouts and queue sizes to avoid long waits. For planning assume capacity for ~150 concurrent sessions across the pool.

5) Cost tradeoffs: H100 pool (3 nodes baseline + 1 buffer) vs A100 pool (4–5 nodes baseline) — we’ll quantify expected monthly committed cost in the proposal.

6) Next steps: Rafael and I will populate the attached sizing worksheet with two options (H100 baseline and A100 baseline) and include estimated monthly committed pricing + burst delta. Marissa — once Jordan confirms the 120 TPS stress target and the ~10% longer medium requests, we’ll finalize numbers.

Happy to jump on a quick 30m call if you want to walk through the worksheet.

Thanks,
